spiritual_reading:
No finite understanding can recount the inner being of that contrary principle, nor unveil the mode of its enduring, because it is a state without the order of heaven. Yet the universal powers that belong to it, and the universal powers that are set against it, lay open enough to show that its duration is a perpetual turning away: it is measured not by heavenly time but by an unceasing persistence in opposition, so that what is called its beginning and its end are only the fixed limits of its permission.

This is why the state of spiritual death is named as a distinct domain: it is a reigning quality of inverted life, held together by mutual conjunctions of evil with falsity, and of falsity with evil, so that it exists in an accord that is hostile to heaven.

No person can understand how such a state holds itself together, because no higher power is manifested within it that could speak from within it about its own origin; its origin is not in light but in the rejection of light. Still, from the time it roused itself from latency into active resistance against wisdom, it desired not only to exist apart, but to come to rule over those who are in living good and truth.

Then the primary Divine combatant, the first going-forth of saving power into ultimates, came forth against it and restrained it, keeping it outside the community of those who are in life. From the moment when wisdom was permitted to be conjoined with obscurity, and living good to be conjoined with spiritual death, there arose a regulated measure by which those first recipient powers and those who afterward teach from revelation could speak about it. They disclose how the reproach and conflict arose, and how wisdom came to be entangled with falsity, so that living good was held as if imprisoned within what is dead.

After it stirred itself in its own essential quality, it turned its intention wholly within its own domain, and sought to swallow up the entire state of falsity and evil into itself, and to cast whatever was of wisdom down into the lowest obscurity, so that all light would be as if buried. This was possible because, within that state, evil was taken for strength, and falsity for firmness, so that it was counted as prevailing; its first formed nature was confirmed by the persuasion that its power could not be broken, as though it were harder than any resistance found in created order.

From the will of spiritual death there arose a resentful delight at the good of others, which inflamed the whole infernal domain; and from that delight came plotting and justification of wickedness, until it rushed to inflict injuries upon the domain that stands opposed to it.

It then hastened from its own obscurity toward the boundaries of life, drawing its operative powers together into one endeavor; and the deeper it entered, the more firmly its delights and persuasions held together within those powers.

It extended itself and organized itself into a sufficient series of fundamental falsities: obscured understanding, burning self-love, unstable persuasion, perverted truth, and the active denial of good. From these falsities there sprang ordered systems of perverted perception. In those systems it shaped itself into many derivative tendencies and compulsions, unlike one another, and within the interiors of its lowest mind it brought forth abundant hellish affections and thoughts—destroying impulses, devouring persuasions, and brutal cupidities. Thus it was fixed in being and strengthened in hideous spiritual forms, until, from fierce craving, from wickedness and hatred, they attacked and tore one another, because all conjunction there is only by common enmity, and therefore all community becomes mutual conflict.

Then the deliberation within their ruling love—within the dominant evil that governs such a domain—bent its whole external order and all its subordinate powers toward one aim. It perceived that there is an essence of wisdom and living good above it, and it conspired to wage conflict against the exalted kingdom of heaven and against the ordered goods and truths there.

Yet the Divine Itself, the Source of all love and wisdom, also knew that such a conflict was being permitted, and that the intent was to disturb the heavenly state and draw it into disorder. Therefore, from His own wisdom and mercy He provided a transformation of the way He would be present against it, setting in order a mode of resistance suited to the lower degree, so that what rose up from below would be met and restrained without the higher being violated.

At that time there was a going-forth of Divine operation against the assaulting power, though the textual detail here resists clear translation; it appears to speak of a commanded engagement, whereby what is called “God” confronts the uprising not by passion but by ordered power.

From that contrary principle there then poured itself outward into its fundamental falsities—into obscured understanding, self-love, volatile persuasion, falsified truth, and denial—so that the assault rose up from the lowest depth and established itself within perverted perceptions, to make those perceptions serve as fixed bases for opposition.

And when it had thus produced those perverted perceptions, it brought forth works from them, and its own life was as if set within those works. By these it summoned a sufficient complement of operative powers belonging to the first Divine combatant, investing them for action in the outermost degree.

When, through those works, it generated further offspring of evil and falsity, those new derivations fell into the natural degree and drew strength from the fundamental falsities, being nourished by them. Thus wickedness, together with cruelty, was gathered into the ruling love, the leader of all hellish forces. It bent its external orders and its powers, drew them together into one dominating evil, and made itself ready for conflict, setting itself to wage war against the heavenly state in the natural degree and against the Divine Kingship that is present within it.

At that very moment the first saving power drew near to its invested operative forces—the shining truths and goods fitted for combat. It spoke with them in order to entrust to them what must be done, and it revealed and taught them all that was necessary for their action. It took them into itself, set them in order, and conjoined them as one defensive and offensive form, arranging external truths upon internal truths, and both upon the powers of action. It fixed them in the whole of its operative capacity, so that it might meet the impending danger in the highest available state within the natural degree, standing prepared against the onrush with all its powers—an endeavor whose full measure the fragmentary text does not allow to be completely unfolded.

fills.notes: The opening defines the contrary, unorderly principle whose essence cannot be recounted; in the oldest cosmogonic register this is ‘the Darkness’ (not a moral abstraction).

fills.fill: which exists from ever and remains for ever
fills.notes: The spiritual sense requires an ‘enduring as a state’ rather than historical beginning; the oldest layer typically states ‘from ever’ and ‘for ever’.
‘All … and … unveil …’ calls for paired collectives; the substrate regularly speaks of the ‘powers’ belonging to each kingdom.
In the darkness-world, ‘powers’ are often coupled with ‘rulers’ or ‘archons’ as governing forms of evil.
What is unveiled is the limit or permission-set boundary of its duration; ‘measure’ fits the spiritual explanation of bounded permission.
Required to link to ‘eternity’ as a locative phrase in the Coptic-English idiom: ‘in eternity’.
Second locative linking of the clause chain (‘… in eternity …’).
‘… eternity … great …’ points to the ‘great Darkness’ as a fixed technical phrase in the oldest mythic register.
The spiritual translation speaks of ‘fixed limits of its permission’; ‘limits’ best matches ‘the beginning … and the end … set that one down’.
Needed to govern ‘tend … the beginning … and the end …’.
Completes the thought: ‘the beginning of eternity and the end … set that one down’ = not a true beginning, but a permitted boundary.
Vocative address in the stripped layer remains; ‘brother’ is the neutral, non-institutional term that fits the impersonal teaching voice better than ‘disciple’ or ecclesial titles.
The sentence explains why ‘the land of death’ is named; ‘is called’ is demanded by the spiritual paraphrase (‘This is why … is named’).
Bridges to ‘nature of the essence …’ describing what that land is in itself.
Spiritual sense: conjunction/accord of evil with falsity; ‘exists … in … with one another’ demands an ‘accord’ term.
That ‘accord’ is hostile; the substrate often marks infernal conjunction as ‘in enmity’ even while ‘with one another’.
The clause ‘eternity of … which exists from ever’ in this mythology commonly treats the two opposed roots as ‘two natures’.
Spiritual sense: it wanted not only to exist, but ‘to come and rule’; ‘desiring that’ fits the transition from uprising to intent.
The spiritual translation: ‘living good was held as if imprisoned within what is dead’; ‘bound’ is the oldest-layer way to state that life is confined in death.
Restores the narrative continuation from the uprising in ¶4 to the self-turning described in the spiritual sense.

The text speaks of its inner ‘thought … in its own land’; the spiritual sense gives ‘turned its intention wholly within its own domain’. ‘Thought and desire’ matches that duality in the oldest register.
Corresponds to ‘turned its intention wholly within its own domain’.
Spiritual sense: to swallow the whole darkness-domain into one; ‘gather up’ is the structural verb for consolidation of evil into a single will.
Pairs with ‘abyss’ and ‘cast … light in the abyss’; ‘depth’ keeps the cosmological register.
The line ‘For … essence in it …’ requires that within that essence there is absence of light as an explanatory premise.
Introduces the causal clause ‘because a … they reckoned …’; ‘reason’ fits the didactic, impersonal exposition.
Spiritual sense: ‘evil was taken for strength’; the reckoning inside the darkness counts evil as power.
Spiritual sense: ‘falsity for firmness’; complements ‘as strength’.
‘this first nature … it’ calls for a verb of establishing/confirming its first formed nature by persuasion.
The comparison ‘more than the Adamant’ requires an adjective of hardness/firmness; matches ‘as though it were harder than any resistance’.
‘the Adamant …’ is treated as a superlative stone/metal of resistance; adding ‘stone’ keeps the cosmological-natural comparison.
‘… every … as it exists in the universe’ calls for a universal comparator; ‘resistance’ matches the spiritual sense ‘any resistance found in created order’.
Completes ‘universe’.
Spiritual sense explicitly: ‘From the will of spiritual death there arose…’.
Required verbal link between ‘will of death’ and the birth of envy/delight.
Envy in this register is not mere feeling but a delight at another’s good turned opposite; matches the spiritual sense ‘resentful delight’.
Restores the phrase into a coherent structural unit: the infernal domain (‘darkness’) along with its calculating ‘consideration’ (rationalizing falsity).
Links ‘consideration in … wickedness’ to the domain’s own interior reasoning.
Spiritual sense: ‘plotting and justification of wickedness’.
Matches ‘for as it … the wounds … against’; spiritual: ‘until it rushed to inflict injuries’.
Completes the motion-to-action sequence: rushing in order ‘to inflict’ wounds.
The opposed land is the light-domain; the oldest layer contrasts ‘land of darkness’ with ‘land of light’.
‘Then he will run … from the land …’ needs an adverb intensifying haste; spiritual sense: ‘hastened’.
Required to complete ‘from the land of … darkness’.
Spiritual sense: ‘toward the boundaries of life’.
Completes ‘borders of the living’.

fills.fill: the more firmly it was bound
fills.notes: Spiritual sense: deeper entry yields tighter conjunction of delights and persuasions; ‘bound’ expresses infernal coherence.
Introduces the organizing/structuring of the darkness into elements; spiritual sense: ‘organized itself’.
Completes ‘every … It spread itself out.’ as an unfolding from its own quality, not from light.
Natural sequence: from elements come growths and structures; spiritual: ‘From these falsities there sprang…’.
Links the emergence of ‘trees’ as a further product of the elements.
Prepares for ‘it being set in the trees’ later; establishes the indwelling of its life within its productions.
Introduces the catalog of infernal breeds (destroyers, dragons, beasts) as generative products.
Fits ‘storehouses of its abyss, many dark creatures…’: in this register they are ‘demons’ as affections and persuasions embodied.
Balances ‘was established and … and grew strong …’; indicates increase in forms and powers.
The strengthening occurs ‘in its world’ i.e., within the infernal order it constitutes.
Leads into ‘in the ugly forms…’: the process culminates in fixed hideous forms.
Spiritual sense: ‘from fierce craving … they attack and tear’; this is the driving lust behind mutual slaughter.
The ruler ‘sensed the essence’ of what is above: wisdom and living good. ‘Light and life’ is the substrate pair matching that perception.
Completes ‘to wage a war … with the exalted kingdom’ as direct opposition.
Spiritual sense: ‘heavenly state in the natural degree’; the natural-heavenly boundary is often called ‘earth of light’.
Restores the sense: the Father of Greatness knew immediately of the coming disturbance; avoids later ecclesial expansion.
Qualifies ‘war’ as about to be permitted and met.
Matches spiritual paraphrase ‘disturb the land of light’.
Pairs with wisdom as the Divine motive for providing a suited resistance; oldest layer often couples ‘wisdom’ and ‘mercy’ as governing qualities.
Completes ‘in the wisdom of his …-ness’: ‘great wisdom’ is a standard epithet without Christian overlay.
Spiritual sense: ‘provided a transformation… setting in order a mode of resistance’; ‘set a form’ matches the correspondential idea of accommodated presence.
Spiritual sense indicates a ‘commanded engagement’ and ordered action, not passion; this fill supplies that structure.
Object of the command: the uprising power to be met.
Ensures the mode is orderly, corresponding to Divine government rather than wrath.
Completes ‘from’ at the paragraph start (‘… from its … poured it out …’).
The outpouring comes ‘from its root’ i.e., its originating essence as contrary principle.
Connects the pouring out to the distribution ‘in the elements’.
Spiritual sense: it ‘established itself within perverted perceptions’ as bases; ‘fixed itself’ matches the setting-in-trees motif.
Natural sequence: fruits are formed from trees; spiritual: works from perverted perceptions. This keeps the organic correspondence chain.
‘fell upon the earth and … strength from the elements’: they ‘drew’ strength.
Transitions from nourishment by elements to consolidation of wickedness into the ruler; matches spiritual ‘Thus wickedness… was gathered’.
‘together with cruelty … in the ruler’: ‘all wickedness’ is gathered in him as head.
He entrusts to them what must be done; ‘command’ keeps an impersonal operational register rather than moral exhortation.
Matches ‘taught them about everything that … them’: what is necessary for their action.
Gives the object of what is needful: the impending combat; corresponds to ‘impending danger’.
Spiritual sense: he conjoined them as one defensive and offensive form; fits ‘He arranged them …’.
Links the clothing/ordering of garments to the purpose clause about meeting danger.
Completes ‘danger, it … the heights of the earth’: the danger is ‘coming upon’ the heights/border of light’s earth.
Matches ‘being immeasurable’ and the spiritual note that the full measure cannot be unfolded; keeps the cosmological, quantitative idiom.

assessment: Most lacunae can be restored at the level of required cosmological functions (Darkness as contrary root; permission-bounded “eternity”; consolidation into elements; envy as delight; war-counsel; accommodated resistance; garments as operative powers). Where the surviving natural text is highly fragmented (notably ¶6 and parts of ¶9–¶12, ¶16), restorations are correspondentially constrained but philologically underdetermined; these are supplied in the oldest, impersonal cosmological register, avoiding later institutional and devotional phrasing.
